title: Tell whether a name is a builtin, alias, function or program
summary: Ask the shell what kind of command a typed word is: a command built into the shell, an alias (a nickname for another command), a function, or a separate program file. This only reads information and changes nothing.

aliases.text: is cd a builtin or program
is ls a program or builtin
what kind of command is cd
check if command is an alias
builtin or program how to tell
is it a shell function or a program
как узнать встроенная ли это команда
какой тип у команды в терминале

steps.explain: Run type followed by the word you want to check. The shell answers in one line and does not run the command. If nothing matches, it says 'not found'.

placeholders.name: NAME
placeholders.description: The word to check: a command name such as cd, ls or ll

steps.expect: cd: 'cd is a shell builtin' (part of the shell). ls: 'ls is /usr/bin/ls' (a path = separate program). 'is aliased to' (bash) or 'is an alias for' (zsh) = alias; 'is a function' = function.

alternatives.explain: Show every match in the order the shell looks, not only the first one. Use it when a name may exist in more than one place.
alternatives.expect: One line per match, for example 'ls is /usr/bin/ls' and then 'ls is /bin/ls'. A shell builtin or alias appears on its own line before the file paths.

alternatives.explain: Standard POSIX form of the same check. Works in bash and zsh, so it is safe to use on macOS and on Linux.
alternatives.expect: One line that names the kind of command, for example 'cd is a shell builtin'.

source.title: type manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
